formatNotes: Inaugural CrossFit Games. No qualification process - anyone could register and compete. Three individual events over two days; the first event was kept secret and drawn at random on the morning of competition from a 'hopper' (a peanut roaster filled with colored balls), reflecting Greg Glassman's belief that the fittest athlete should be ready for any task. On-site scaling was permitted and scaled scores were ranked below Rx on the leaderboard. Overall placing was determined by points across the three events (archived leaderboard shows a 100-points-for-first style table: Fitzgerald won with 272, Gentry with 290); the exact 2007-era points table was never formally published. Individual champions each received 500 dollars. An affiliate team competition (won by CrossFit Santa Cruz) ran the same weekend but is not part of the individual record. Field counts are starters per the official leaderboard archive (44 men, 20 women): every listed athlete recorded a score in at least one event, so all 44 men and 20 women are counted as starters. Several athletes withdrew from individual events (e.g. three men, including Keegan Martin, show WD on the hopper workout but scored the CrossFit Total or trail run; five women show WD on one or two events), so per-event starter counts are lower than the overall field. Roughly 70 athletes attended in total with about 150 spectators.
yearSummary: The first CrossFit Games were a grassroots gathering on Dave Castro's family ranch in Aromas, California, with no qualifiers, roughly 70 athletes, and a 500 dollar prize per champion. Programming established themes that would define the sport: an unknown-and-unknowable element (the hopper-drawn row/pull-up/push-jerk triplet), a pure monostructural test (an approximately 5K trail run over the ranch's steep hills), and a pure strength test (the CrossFit Total of back squat, press, and deadlift maxes). James Fitzgerald (OPT) took the men's title on consistency - second in both day-one events - while Jolie Gentry won the hopper workout outright and finished second in the other two to dominate the women's field. Every movement contested was by definition a Games debut, and the hopper workout proved iconic enough to be recreated as the event '2007' at the 2013 Games.

events.name: Hopper-Style CrossFit WOD
events.description:
For time:
1,000-meter row (Concept-2)
Then, 5 rounds of:
25 pull-ups
7 push jerks (135 lb men / 85 lb women)

The workout was drawn at random on the morning of competition from a hopper (a peanut roaster filled with colored balls). On-site scaling was permitted: leaderboard scores show men scaling to 95 lb jerks and/or jumping pull-ups, and women to 65 lb.
events.notes: First event ever contested at a CrossFit Games. Women's load conflict: the archived official games.crossfit.com workout page and WODwell list 85 lb; the Wikipedia article says 95 lb - the official source (85 lb) is used here. No official time cap is documented; athletes who did not finish were recorded by round/rep progress (e.g. 'Rnd 5 25 Pullups') and the slowest recorded finish was exactly 20:00, suggesting a cutoff near 20 minutes, but this is unconfirmed. Brett Marshall (AFT) won the men's event using butterfly pull-ups; overall champion James Fitzgerald was second (13:39). The workout was recreated as event '2007' at the 2013 Games (there with a 15-minute cap).

events.name: Trail Run
events.description:
Trail run, approximately 5 kilometers (about 3 miles), for time.
Off-road course over the steep, hilly terrain of the Castro family ranch in Aromas. No added load. Contested in the afternoon of day one, after the hopper workout.
events.notes: Exact course length was never published; the official archived workout page lists it only as 'Trail run (approximately 5 k)'. Chris Spealler edged overall champion James Fitzgerald (20:45) by two seconds.

events.name: CrossFit Total
events.description:
CrossFit Total - sum of the heaviest successful single repetition in each of:
Back squat, 1-rep max
Shoulder press, 1-rep max
Deadlift, 1-rep max

Loads were athlete-selected maximal attempts (no prescribed weights). Per Wikipedia, athletes had up to 3 attempts at each lift, taken within 4-minute windows. Score is the combined total in pounds.
events.notes: First pure strength test at the Games, using Mark Rippetoe's CrossFit Total benchmark (CrossFit Journal, 2006). The 3-attempts-per-lift / 4-minute-window detail comes from Wikipedia and could not be verified against an official source. Loads array is empty because all weights were athlete-selected maxes. Olympic lifter Josh Everett was second among men (1133 lb); event winner Connor Banks finished 14th overall after placing 31st in both day-one events. Leaderboard spells the women's winner 'Nichole Dehart' (Wikipedia uses 'Nicole').
